## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Lotte Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [Juli 1940], SZ-AAL/B1.30
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.30
- Datum: 07.1940
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 5 Scans

pages.transcription:
Hanne In your quality as our locum tenant please buy atonce
our birthday present for Manfred, 6 nice music books //
Dear Hanna u Manfred,
Stefan has thanked you so beautifully
that I need not repeat it but just confirm
everything he has said. I hope that the
house will not only give you trouble but
also some pleasure and that you consider
it as another home and not as a respon-
sibility. Much as I am glad to go I
hate to leave you and your family
and to be away from home. And as my
imagination is very poor, it is fairly easy
for me to overlook the next time and to
look forward to the day of our home-
coming and on that day all may come to
the station, you, the Rosemount family
and even all the Mayers and Altmanns.
But in the meantime I shall not forget
the realities and do my very best to settle
Eva and to make all necessary enquiries.
Kindest regards to all and thanks
again and auf baldiges Wiedersehen
Lotte
Stefan says it is so easy to write in the running train,
I hope you can read it.
"Wilson file" is in the red cardboard file in the office,
called "Uebersetzung".
The Balzac MS is, I believe, in the study and in the
files. There are always 4 copies together, you would have to sort
them out.
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Lotte Zweig. Der Text am linken Rand und am unteren Rand ist nachträglich hinzugefügt. Die Anmerkung am unteren Rand bezieht sich auf die Organisation von Unterlagen.
Rückseite des ersten Blattes, zeigt den durchscheinenden Text der Vorderseite (bleed-through).

pages.transcription:
Dear Hannah, I wish to thank you for all the
trouble you will have with our house and other
affairs. Take nothing whatever serious. There are
in this moment thousands and hundred thousands
of men abroad and her matters have to wait, why
not just mine? Nothing is important than the
health of you all and I hope that with the com-
bination of Levin that all will go smoothly and
Manfred have his well deserved holiday. You
may imagine what good feeling it means to us
that we know all our affairs in the best hands and
I should be glad, if we could do something for
you all. You know that besides all my pessimism
which sees the things before they happen, there is a
good deal of optimism and I believe we will have
after some months of uncertainty again a fairly
quiet time; whatever happens after this war it will
easier to be bear than the continuous expectation of
evil and murderous surprise. Give my love to your
husband, your daughter, mother in law, sister and
brother and niece and to the whole house; we
will not forget you as far as we may be for
some time! Yours
Stefan
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Stefan Zweig. Der Text ist auf einem separaten Blatt geschrieben.
Rückseite des zweiten Blattes, zeigt den durchscheinenden Text der Vorderseite (bleed-through).

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, die Handschrift von Lotte und Stefan Zweig ist klar erkennbar. Die wenigen Korrekturen im Text (wie 'than' über der Zeile) wurden gemäß den Regeln transkribiert.
